_comment: Follow-up golden set for `engrex eval --set eval/conversations.json`. Each case is the next
message in a conversation: 'history' is what came before, 'question' is the follow-up as a user
would actually type it, and 'relevant' is what that follow-up needs. Kept separate from
golden.json so its numbers stay comparable to earlier baselines.
Run it twice, once with --raw-followups (search the follow-up verbatim) and once without
(condense it first, as chat does). The follow-up slice is the comparison that matters.
Like golden.json these are STARTER cases over this repo's docs/. Replace them with follow-ups
you actually ask, especially ones where the follow-up shares no words with what it needs.

history.content: what file formats can engrex ingest?
Engrex ingests plain text, markdown, PDF, DOCX, PPTX, HTML, and common code and data files dropped into ~/Engrex.

cases.question: how does it handle the slides one?
cases.note: Reference resolution: 'the slides one' means PPTX. Nothing retrievable in the raw follow-up.

history.content: There are three read-only tools: search_notes, get_document, and query_knowledge_graph.

cases.question: what does the first one return?

history.content: which listeners does the daemon run?
The daemon runs a Unix socket, an HTTP server, a graph server, and a file watcher.

cases.question: and what's the second one for?
cases.note: Ordinal reference to the HTTP server.

history.content: how does hybrid search combine vector and keyword results?
It fuses the vector ranking and the BM25 keyword ranking with Reciprocal Rank Fusion.

cases.question: why does the keyword half drop some words?
cases.note: Topic shift within the same document: stopword removal. Has some retrievable words on its own.

history.content: how fast is the HNSW index compared to brute force?
It is faster at larger corpus sizes, but recall depends on efSearch.

cases.question: what happens to recall as the corpus grows?
cases.note: Implicit subject: 'the corpus' only means the HNSW benchmark in context.

history.content: what happens when I edit and re-save a file that was already ingested?
Unchanged content is skipped by its hash; changed content has its old chunks deleted and is re-ingested.

cases.question: can that ever create two copies of it?
cases.note: Points at the identity trap section. 'that' and 'it' carry the whole subject.

cases.question: what does search_notes return?
cases.note: Standalone control: the condensed and raw runs should score identically here.
